about: Earlier names allowed in the repository, where, and why. Read by scripts/check_names.py; explained in docs/kept-names.md. kind: contract = a name another program we do not build expects; data = a value already stored or deployed; fallback = an earlier name still read so old installs and deployments keep working; record = a statement of origin that must name it; guard = a test that checks an earlier name is gone.

rules.reason: The app's notice states where the window and shell come from and who made them.
The explanation of this list names every earlier name it checks for.
The documents name the kept identifiers they explain: the provider id, the Connect service, the earlier data folder and setting, the Render runner service and desktop file names.
The website's demo is the app's window: the upstream compiled renderer, patched. Its internal identifiers are the upstream bytes.
The upstream app's own dependency list (@anysphere/* packages) that the pinned renderer and shell were built with; the identity fields are Simeon's.
Bootstrap and the package checks read the upstream 0.18.0 app by its real name, download address and executable (Grok Bot.app, Grok_Bot_0.18.0.dmg, Contents/MacOS/Grok Bot).

The window patch finds the upstream strings (Grok Bot, New Bot, Caisra, the .sand-grok-bot-mark class) to replace them, counts the upstream maker's name left after the brand pass, and its tests feed it those strings.
The packager renames the upstream shell's executable and helper bundles, which are named Grok Bot, to Simeon.
The packager recognises the upstream maker's names in Info.plist strings in order to replace them.
Generated protocol code: service, message and field names the pinned window and the server speak on the wire (aiserver.v1.GrokBotService, Xai* messages).
The server answers the Connect service aiserver.v1.GrokBotService, and the GROK_BOT source enum ("grok-bot" in JSON) the app sends with a cloud agent.
Settings are read as SIMEON_<NAME> and the earlier CLAIDOR_<NAME> is still read, so deployments keep working while their variables are renamed.
Sessions, tokens, custom-domain records, placeholder e-mails and webhook headers made before the rename carry the earlier name and are still accepted (or still sent).
The data folder was ~/.caisra (with a .grokbot-data-root-v1 marker); the first start moves it to ~/.simeon, and the earlier folder stays protected from the local-exec daemon.
A testing Docker box made before the rename carries the earlier owner label and is still recognised, so it is replaced cleanly.
The app's sign-in callback scheme was caisra:// before simeon://; a build from before the rename can still finish a sign-in.
Meter event names and Composio user ids already stored under the earlier name.
A real S3 bucket that serves images; renaming it means moving the files first.
A published npm package (@spaire/sdk) the checkout imports; its name is not ours to change.

Database migrations are the history of the live schema: table and column names they created (court_decisions.ohadata_code, the tie-out tables) exist in the database, and a past migration's text is not rewritten.

The Render blueprint keeps the service names, the CLAIDOR_ variable keys and the repository address that exist on Render until they are changed there (a renamed service in the blueprint would be a new, empty service).

Names the pinned window, the generated protocol code or the upstream agent code read or send: the Connect service and its source enum, the account status field isAnysphereUser the window reads, upstream model ids (grok-4.5) that saved agents carry, the window's mark class and state attribute, feature-gate and prompt-flag names, the MCP OAuth extension id and a summary kind stored in conversation state.
Generated from, or a record of, the upstream app's own bytes: the feature-gate table and the evidence files that list its strings and offsets.

Earlier names still recognised on a Mac: the upstream app's user-data folder (Grok Bot) and data markers the first start migrates from, the token folder path an older box mounted (still refused to attachments), and "Grok", the upstream default agent name a saved agent may carry.
The model provider id was "claidor" and its settings SAND_CLAIDOR_* until 29 September 2026; stored settings, usage and transcripts on a Mac still carry the old id, and both setting names are read.
A cloud box made before 29 September 2026 carries the earlier Docker label prefix; its host version is still read from it.

rules.match: doesNotMatch|never reads|no longer|Claidor account|Sign in to Claidor|Claidor sign-in|Claidor API|Sign In with Claidor
rules.reason: Tests that check an earlier name is gone from what a person or the agent reads have to name it.
The server and web app are derived from Polar (Apache 2.0); the licence and notice name it.

A stand-in that forwards the old start commands (polar.app:app, polar.worker.run) to the simeon package, because Render keeps each service's start command in its own settings. Remove once every Render service starts simeon.*.
polar-sdk is a published Python package the server's SDK test uses (its client class is Polar); its name is not ours.

Values already stored, deployed or published under the earlier name: Prometheus metric names and the Grafana dashboards that query them, Redis keys, Stripe idempotency keys, S3 object metadata and the upstream's public image bucket the e-mails still load, the Logfire project, the production JWK id, the PostHog anonymous id, a CSV import column, API field and OpenAPI extension names the web client reads, the X-Polar-* response headers, the web app's earlier env names (still read after SIMEON_*), and a charting library's own class name.
Links to the upstream issue or pull request that explains the code next to them.
